QOP.label: NHS Greater Manchester Integrated Care Board
QOP.summary: Greater Manchester has significant unmet need across respiratory, cardiovascular and musculoskeletal pathways. Digital therapeutics are live in COPD and cardiac rehabilitation, with MSK in procurement. The biggest constraint across all three pathways is invitation reach — most eligible patients are never offered the intervention.

opportunities.label: COPD and respiratory
opportunities.priorityRationale: Large eligible cohort with strong NICE-backed evidence. Two live deployments demonstrate proof of model — the opportunity now is scaling invitation reach from 6% to 25%+ of eligible population.

prevalence.context: adults on the QOF COPD register across GM

highRisk.context: patients with ≥2 exacerbations in last 12 months (MRC 3+)

admissions.context: COPD emergency admissions per year across GM acute trusts
admissions.source: SUS extract (GM trusts, ICD J41-J44 primary)

readmissions.context: readmitted within 90 days of a COPD admission

aeAttendances.context: A&E attendances with COPD as primary presenting complaint

costBurden.context: annual COPD emergency admission cost (GM, spell-level HRG average)

gap.headroomStatement: 5,780 eligible patients have never received an invitation. At current registration and activation rates, reaching them would add ~860 active users — more than doubling the monitored cohort.
gap.constraintStatement: The binding constraint is not the product or the evidence — it is systematic invitation at scale across GP practices and community respiratory teams.

opportunities.evidenceStatus: NICE HTG736 recommended; Bradford Teaching Hospitals RWE evaluation; multiple RCTs
opportunities.readinessStatus: Fully assured; buyer pack and implementation guide available

impactCategories.summary: 30–48% reduction in emergency admissions in evaluated cohorts (Bradford, Frimley)
~110 bed-days per year released per 500 monitored patients; 22% fewer A&E presentations
iPad provision programme removes digital exclusion barrier; no correlation between deprivation and activation rates observed
£245k net annual value per 500 patients (central scenario, before licence cost). At full eligible cohort: £4.8m annual opportunity.

opportunities.label: Cardiac rehabilitation
opportunities.priorityRationale: National cardiac rehab uptake is below 50%. GM has 3,200 eligible patients per year with only 47% starting any form of rehab. Digital rehab can extend capacity without building new face-to-face programmes.

prevalence.context: new cardiac events eligible for rehabilitation per year (MI, CABG, PCI, HF diagnosis)

highRisk.context: patients who did NOT start cardiac rehab within 12 months of event

admissions.context: cardiac-related emergency admissions per year (GM trusts)

readmissions.context: readmitted within 12 months of index cardiac event

waitingList.context: median wait from referral to first cardiac rehab session (face-to-face)
waitingList.source: GM cardiac rehab waiting list data (synthetic)

gap.headroomStatement: 1,700 patients per year are eligible but never start rehabilitation in any form. Digital rehab removes the capacity and geography barrier — patients can start within days of discharge rather than waiting 14 weeks.
gap.constraintStatement: Digital cardiac rehab is 6 weeks live in GM. The immediate constraint is early — establishing referral pathways from acute cardiology and embedding digital as a standard offer alongside face-to-face.

opportunities.evidenceStatus: NICE-recommended digital cardiac rehab; NACR-registered programme; 6-minute walk test improvement in early cohort
opportunities.readinessStatus: Early deployment — 6 weeks live; 90-day review pending

impactCategories.summary: +18% improvement in 6-minute walk distance in initial cohort (n=34, early signal)
Each digital place avoids a face-to-face slot. At scale: potential 800+ additional rehab completions/yr without new F2F capacity
Removes waiting list and travel barriers — patients in deprived areas face longest waits for traditional rehab
Not modelled at current scale. Rehab completion is associated with 26% lower readmission (NACR national data).

opportunities.label: MSK and lower back pain
opportunities.priorityRationale: MSK is the largest single referral category for GM community services. Low back pain accounts for 40% of MSK first contacts. A digital self-management programme can absorb demand that currently requires face-to-face physiotherapy slots.

prevalence.context: adults seeking GP care for low back pain per year across GM

highRisk.context: referred to community MSK physiotherapy from primary care

admissions.context: spinal surgery procedures per year (elective, GM trusts)

costBurden.context: community MSK physiotherapy cost (GM, all providers)

waitingList.context: median wait from GP referral to first MSK physio appointment
waitingList.source: GM community provider waiting list returns (synthetic)

gap.headroomStatement: Every patient currently referred for community MSK physiotherapy could be offered a digital self-management programme while waiting, or as an alternative for those with uncomplicated low back pain. Current waiting times of 11 weeks mean patients deteriorate before receiving any intervention.
gap.constraintStatement: No digital MSK product is currently deployed in GM. Procurement for an HTG-assured product (getUMobile) is in progress. The question is not evidence — it is commissioning decision and pathway integration.

opportunities.evidenceStatus: NICE HTG recommended for MSK self-management; multiple RCTs showing equivalence to face-to-face physio for uncomplicated LBP
opportunities.readinessStatus: Product assured. Procurement in progress. Implementation planning with GM MSK leads.

impactCategories.summary: Evidence shows non-inferior outcomes to face-to-face physio for uncomplicated LBP (ODI improvement, pain reduction)
Could absorb 30–50% of new MSK referrals as first-line digital offer, releasing ~4,000 face-to-face physio slots/yr
Immediate access — no 11-week wait. Rural and working patients gain most from flexible digital delivery
Modelled: £3.7m annual opportunity if 40% of new referrals diverted to digital first (central scenario)

GEN.label: NHSE Average ICB
GEN.summary: NHSE Average ICB is an illustrative reference geography for COPD remote monitoring. Figures are synthetic prototype data sized for a mid-scale ICB, so commissioners can explore local value without selecting a named system.

opportunities.label: COPD and respiratory
opportunities.priorityRationale: Illustrative mid-scale COPD cohort with NICE-backed remote monitoring evidence. Early Luscii deployment is live; the opportunity is scaling invitation reach across the high-risk cohort.

prevalence.context: adults on the QOF COPD register (illustrative NHSE Average ICB)
prevalence.source: Synthetic prototype data — NHSE Average ICB reference site

highRisk.context: patients with ≥2 exacerbations in last 12 months (MRC 3+)
highRisk.source: Synthetic prototype data — NHSE Average ICB reference site

admissions.source: Synthetic prototype data — NHSE Average ICB reference site

readmissions.context: readmitted within 90 days of a COPD admission
readmissions.source: Synthetic prototype data — NHSE Average ICB reference site

aeAttendances.context: A&E attendances with COPD as primary presenting complaint
aeAttendances.source: Synthetic prototype data — NHSE Average ICB reference site

costBurden.context: annual COPD emergency admission cost (illustrative, spell-level HRG average)
costBurden.source: National tariff × NHSE Average ICB volume (synthetic)

gap.headroomStatement: About 4,000 high-risk patients have never received an invitation. At current registration and activation rates, reaching them would roughly treble the monitored cohort.
gap.constraintStatement: The binding constraint is systematic invitation at scale across primary care and community respiratory teams — not product assurance or evidence.

opportunities.evidenceStatus: NICE HTG736 recommended; Bradford and Frimley RWE evaluations; multiple RCTs
opportunities.readinessStatus: Fully assured; buyer pack and implementation guide available

impactCategories.summary: 30–48% reduction in emergency admissions in evaluated cohorts (Bradford, Frimley)
~110 bed-days per year released per 500 monitored patients; 16–31% fewer A&E presentations
Remote monitoring reduces travel burden for high-risk patients; digital inclusion support can be layered where needed
£245k net annual value per 500 patients (central scenario, before licence cost). Scaled to NHSE Average ICB high-risk cohort as an illustrative opportunity.
